Berge Rederi Future , a newly established subsidiary of Norwegian family group Berge Rederi , has taken delivery of BRF Froan , a 13,250 DWT coastal self-unloading bulk carrier built by Jiangsu SOHO Marine Heavy Industry in China — a vessel the owner bills as the world's largest battery-powered bulk carrier.
Propulsion is provided entirely by a 23.5 MWh battery package, supplemented by two rotor sails and solar panels mounted on the cargo hatches; charging infrastructure has been installed at both loading and discharge ports to support continuous back-and-forth operations over a roughly 24-hour round voyage of approximately 230 nautical miles. The vessel cost around NOK 500m ($52m), of which NOK 270m was covered by Norwegian state energy agency Enova and the NOx Fund; SpareBank 1 SMN provided the remainder in debt financing. BRF Froan has entered a fixed five-year contract carrying marble for Omya Hustadmarmor between Brønnøy and Visnes and the production plant at Elnesvågen. Annual CO₂ savings are projected at 9,000 tonnes and NOx reductions at 200 tonnes. A sister vessel, BRF Frøya , is due for delivery in 2027.
The order and delivery mark a rare commercial deployment of full battery propulsion on a cargo vessel of this size, backed by a long-term industrial charter that made the economics viable — a model that could attract attention from other short-sea operators weighing zero-emission newbuilds.

Chinese specialists have built the world’s largest electric dry cargo ship, equipped with a 23.5-megawatt-hour battery.
